title: Eternal God, Our Humbled Souls
description: Eternal God, Our Humbled Souls in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 993 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “On Occasion of a Destructive Fire”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal God, our hum-bled souls Be-fore thy pre-sence bow; With all thy wast-ing mag-a-zines, How ter-ri-ble art thou!

lines: And that which we in strength had reared
And blackened walls and smoking heaps
Lord, in this hour we come to thee,
Yet bless the hand of guardian love,
That snatched us from the flame.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
